messages.subject: Warning message
parts:
I received the following warning message:

"Warning: R object of different size than NimArrDouble. R obj has size 1 but NimArrDbl has size 4.”

When running the following code below. The program completes and the MCMC samples seem to be fine, so I’m wondering what is the cause of the warning? Can I ignore the warning?

Thanks,
Brian


maskCode4_3 <- nimbleCode({
### Priors
intercept~dnorm(0,sd=1000)
maleEffect~dnorm(0,sd = 1000)
ageEffect[1] <-0
ageMaleI[1] <-0
sigma_RE ~ dunif(0, 1000)

for(i in 2:4) {
# Priors for age effect and age:male interaction
ageEffect[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
ageMaleI[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
}

for(g in 1:8) {
# Priors for business random effect
b[g] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma_RE)
}

### logit link and Bernoulli data probabilities
for(i in 1:N) {

logit(mask_prob[i]) <- intercept + maleEffect*male[i] +
ageClassBase[i]*ageEffect[ageClass[i]] + male[i]*ageMaleI[ageClass[i]] +
b[bGroup[i]]
mask[i] ~ dbern(mask_prob[i])
}

### Derived quantities
# Odds ratios
maleOdds<-exp(maleEffect)
youngOdds<-exp(ageEffect[2])
middleOdds<-exp(ageEffect[3])
elderOdds<-exp(ageEffect[4])
maleYoungOdds<-exp(ageMaleI[2])
maleMiddleOdds<-exp(ageMaleI[3])
maleElderOdds<-exp(ageMaleI[4])
})


mydataWOna<-mydata[!is.na(mydata$gender_factor) & !is.na(mydata$age_factor),]
maskConsts <- list(N = dim(mydataWOna)[1],
ageClassBase=ifelse(as.integer(mydataWOna$age_factor)>1,1,0),
ageClass=as.integer(mydataWOna$age_factor),
male=as.integer(mydataWOna$gender_factor)-1,
bGroup=as.integer(mydataWOna$business_factor)
)
maskData <- list(mask = mydataWOna$wearing_mask)

maskInits <- list(
list(intercept = 0.5, maleEffect = 0.1,
ageEffect=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3),
ageMaleI=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3)+10,
b=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3,-0.1,-0.5,-0.3,0.4),
sigma_RE=20 ),
list(intercept = 1, maleEffect = 1,
ageEffect=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3)+0.1,
ageMaleI=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3)+0.1,
b=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3,-0.1,-0.5,-0.3,0.4)-10,
sigma_RE=10 ),
list(intercept = 2, maleEffect = -1,
ageEffect=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3)-0.1,
ageMaleI=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3)-0.1,
b=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3,-0.1,-0.5,-0.3,0.4)+10,
sigma_RE=30 ),
list(intercept = -1, maleEffect = -0.1,
ageEffect=0.3,
ageMaleI=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3)-30,
b=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3,-0.1,-0.5,-0.3,0.4)+0.3,
sigma_RE=25+20 )
)


mcmc43.1.out <- nimbleMCMC(code = maskCode4_3, data = maskData, inits = maskInits,
monitors = c("intercept", "maleEffect","ageEffect",
"ageMaleI","b","sigma_RE",
"maleOdds","youngOdds","middleOdds",
"elderOdds","maleYoungOdds","maleMiddleOdds",
"maleElderOdds"),
thin = 100,
niter = 2000000, nburnin=10000,
nchains = 4, setSeed = FALSE,
constants = maskConsts,samplesAsCodaMCMC=TRUE)

parts:
hi Brian,

You're initializing ageEffect with one value instead of four values in the fourth component of the inits list.

chris
